sections.text: Broadcast journalism is news delivered through audio and video media — structurally constrained by time (30-second packages vs. 3,000-word print articles), distribution technology (spectrum licensing, satellite, cable, streaming), and the performance demands of on-camera or on-microphone presentation. The format shapes the journalism: broadcast favors the visual and emotional over the analytical; immediacy over depth; conflict and drama over process.
